newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share prices steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share prices steady in quiet market.

text.p: Nigerian share prices were steady on relatively low trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
The all-share index rose slightly to 8716.59 from 8714.31 on Monday.
"The volume of trade is quiet low and there's nothing to drive the market," said one broker.
Newly-listed Guaranty Trust Bank led the gains, rising 20 kobo to 12.30 naira on expectations it will soon announce good earnings results.
Guiness, which posted improved full-year profits for 1996, rose 15 kobo to 8.65 naira.
Oil stocks were mixed. Mobil, which rose 20 kobo on Monday, gained another 10 on Tuesday to 63.20 naira while African Petroleum fell 20 kobo to 58.20 naira.
FSB Bank continued to rise on expectations it would also post a good corporate result this week. It gained two kobo after rising 19 kobo on Monday and now stands at 4.01 naira.

Law Union and Rock fell 30 kobo, the biggest drop of the day, to 6.15 naira. Construction firm Costain West Africa fell 20 kobo to 3.01, while Evans Medical lost 10 kobo at the second tier market to close at 4.60 naira.
